newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares idle in pre-bourse with weaker dlr.
newsitem.headline: German shares idle in pre-bourse with weaker dlr.

text.p: German shares were on Wednesday unable to build further on the late gains made in post-bourse trade with a stronger Wall Street on Tuesday as dealers said the weaker dollar was holding dealings back.
The IBIS-DAX index of electronic trade stood barely changed, 1.38 points lower at 3,357.88 in early dealings, with June DAX futures unchanged at 3,373.0.

With turnover low and even 1996 result details from Daimler-Benz AG failing to excite the market, dealers saw a narrow day-range, with one saying the DAX index was unlikely to trade much outside 3,340-90.
The dollar traded steadily below the 1.730 mark level at 1.725 marks in early European dealings.

Dealers said new result details released from Daimler-Benz were being viewed positively but not with the same enthusiasm that greeted recent figures from BMW. Upgrades were nonetheless expected to result from an analyst meeting later today.

Daimler's shares were traded five pfennigs higher in IBIS trade to 139.35 just before bourse open after earlier reaching an all-time high of 142.40. Turnover, at 710,000 shares dealt, was the highest of the day so far but not seen as exceptional.
Dealers said a move by the group to issue 1.1 billion marks in mandatory convertible notes to strengthen its capital base was not being seen positively.
Drugs group Schwarz Pharma, which late Tuesday said group net profits rose 14.4 percent in 1996 and further a profit growth was expected in 1997, rose 3.50 marks to 137.0.
